## Problem Essence

`Igel._process_data` currently converts whatever columns arrive into an array after preprocessing, without applying or saving a raw-feature selection. Consequently later data can have a different order or extra or missing columns, while neither the model nor `description.json` records the raw input contract.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`igel/preprocessing.py`**: `read_data_to_df` and the preprocessing helpers operate on DataFrames. This is the natural location for fitting a raw schema and aligning later DataFrames to it before encoding, imputation, and scaling.
- **`igel/igel.py`**: `__init__` resolves paths and training metadata; `_process_data` handles all input routes; `fit` saves the model and description; `evaluate` and `_get_predictions` call the model; and `export` currently hard-codes an input width of four. Trace all of these together.
- **`igel/configs.py`**: defines results paths and the default and available dataset properties. Add consistent feature-option defaults and a schema artifact path here.
- **`igel/constants.py`**: centralizes artifact filenames; define the schema filename alongside the model and description filenames.
- **`igel/servers/fastapi_server.py`**: `/predict` writes request data and invokes `Igel`; translate schema validation errors into HTTP 400 with a JSON detail and clean up the temporary file.

## Solution Approach

Treat the ordered raw feature schema as a training artifact, distinct from the transformed model-input width. During fit, derive it once from raw data and feature options, save it alongside the model, and summarize it in the description. During evaluation and prediction, load that same artifact and reconstruct the ordered canonical raw inputs before the existing preprocessing and before any model call.

Keep supervised targets separate from raw features, including when there are multiple targets; clustering has no targets. A common selection/alignment path is important so the CLI and API do not implement different rules. The description should expose the artifact path, selected input names, categorized dropped names, and canonical-to-alias mapping.

## Implementation Directions

1. In the configuration and constants modules, establish defaults for `include`, `exclude`, `drop_constant`, and `drop_duplicate`, plus the schema artifact filename and results path. Check both default and available dataset property dictionaries.
2. In preprocessing, normalize and validate the options against **raw** column names. Choose candidates in include order when provided, otherwise in dataset order; exclude candidates, then optionally drop constants and duplicate columns. Preserve the first surviving duplicate as canonical and record later names as its aliases. Return both the selected DataFrame and enough metadata to apply the same contract later.
3. Add a complementary alignment operation that visits canonical names in saved order. Accept a canonical column or any recorded alias, compare all supplied sources row-wise when more than one is present, and construct a canonical-named DataFrame. Ignore unrelated columns and report missing canonical names and conflicting sources clearly.
4. Integrate schema fitting into `_process_data` immediately after reading raw data, before the existing encoding and missing-value handling. Separate targets first, then combine them as needed for the existing supervised preprocessing and split logic. On evaluate and predict, load and apply the saved schema instead of fitting a new one. Follow the clustering evaluation route carefully: it currently calls `_prepare_clustering_data`, which is also used for fitting, so it must not relearn a schema from evaluation data.
5. Save the schema after successful model fitting and include its path and metadata in `fit_description`. Resolve the path when loading a trained model, including any supported explicit path overrides. Consider how older descriptions without an artifact should behave rather than silently using arbitrary new input columns.
6. Ensure validation exceptions propagate through `_process_data`, `evaluate`, and `_get_predictions`; these currently log and swallow exceptions. At the server boundary, map schema validation failures to HTTP 400 while retaining cleanup. Check that evaluation honors the supplied model path as well.
7. For export, read the training description instead of using the literal four. Distinguish raw selected-feature count from the width after transformations such as one-hot encoding; use recorded transformed width or training shape where appropriate.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- Reject unknown names, duplicate entries within either option, empty or non-string names, and target names in either option. Reject a configuration that leaves no inputs. Decide and test the behavior of an empty include list consistently.
- Test include order, overlap between include and exclude, and deterministic ordering of all dropped lists and aliases. Constant detection and duplicate comparison should handle missing values deliberately and consistently; comparisons must cover every row.
- Exercise canonical-only, alias-only, multiple agreeing sources, conflicting aliases, missing required features, and extra raw columns. Check error messages name the relevant columns and verify the model is not called on invalid input.
- Test single-target, multi-target, and clustering fit, evaluate, and predict paths, plus `/predict` status and JSON detail. Verify both the joblib artifact and description fields after a fresh fit and check path overrides.
- Existing encoding, imputation, and scaling are fitted again on incoming data in this code; raw schema persistence alone does not make those transformations persistent. Be careful not to imply otherwise or confuse raw input count with transformed width.
- The reference also adjusts the CV estimator fallback and hyperparameter-search return ordering. Inspect their existing interfaces if touching those nearby paths rather than accidentally introducing unrelated regressions.
- Extend the existing tests under `tests/test_igel` with focused schema unit tests and end-to-end cases; use isolated temporary results directories so artifacts from one run cannot mask another.

## Problem Essence

Ink currently exposes only `flex` and `none` in its style type, and its display adapter sends every value other than `flex` to Yoga as hidden. The rendering pipeline relies on Yoga's computed flex geometry, so accepting a new string alone cannot parse grid tracks, place children, or calculate the output dimensions needed to render them.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`src/styles.ts`** — `Styles` defines the public style surface, including existing gaps and display; `applyDisplayStyles` maps display values to Yoga. Add the grid-facing types here and ensure grid remains visible to Yoga. `Box` derives its props from `Styles` and forwards them as its style (`src/components/Box.tsx`), so this type is also the public entry point.
- **`src/grid-layout.ts`** — This is a new module in the reference patch, not an existing repository file. It owns template and placement interpretation, intrinsic measurement, track sizing, occupancy and placement, and translating grid geometry into Yoga child geometry. It traverses the DOM to find grid containers.
- **`src/renderer.ts`** — The normal renderer creates an `Output` from the computed root dimensions and then traverses the layout. The reference integrates grid resolution before output allocation and considers descendant bottoms when determining output height, so automatically created rows are not lost below the buffer.

Useful supporting locations: `src/dom.ts` stores each element's full style and Yoga node and shows how text is measured; `src/reconciler.ts` stores and applies styles at creation and update; `src/ink.tsx` and `src/render-to-string.ts` calculate Yoga layout before rendering; `src/render-node-to-output.ts` reads parent-relative Yoga coordinates and performs clipping. `test/gap.tsx` demonstrates the existing rendering-test style.

## Solution Approach

Keep Yoga responsible for the surrounding flex layout and use an additional grid pass once container dimensions are available. The reference maps grid containers to a visible Yoga display, then interprets the retained DOM styles itself; it assigns the resulting cell rectangles to child Yoga nodes and recalculates layout before output is drawn. This connects the public types, the sizing and placement algorithm, and the renderer rather than treating them as independent changes.

Represent track definitions in a form that distinguishes fixed, fractional, automatic, and min/max tracks. Determine placements before sizing content-dependent tracks, then resolve the two axes independently using the container's inner dimensions and the appropriate gap. Finally, compute positions and span dimensions from the resolved tracks, including intervening gaps, and ensure an auto-height grid and its output buffer have enough height.

## Implementation Directions

1. In `Styles`, investigate the display union and add the two template properties and the two item placement properties with types matching the issue. Adjust the Yoga display mapping so that `none` still hides, while grid is not accidentally hidden. Confirm that Box's existing prop forwarding exposes the additions without a separate prop list.
2. Design a tokenizer that separates tracks on whitespace outside parentheses, so `minmax(2, 1fr)` remains one track. Parse fixed numbers, `fr`, `auto`, and the specified `minmax` forms; do not expand the scope to `repeat()`, named lines, or configurable auto flow.
3. Convert the public 1-based item positions to an internal representation. A range denotes grid lines, so its span is the difference between end and start. Track occupied cells for explicit placements and assign remaining children in row order, extending rows as necessary. Consider how an item with only one axis specified should be handled and test it explicitly.
4. Calculate usable track space after subtracting borders, padding and gaps. Resolve fixed and intrinsic auto sizes and reserve all minimums before distributing leftover space by fractional weight, including fractional `minmax` maxima. For example, after minimums and gaps consume 6 cells of a 16-cell inner axis, `minmax(2, 1fr)` and `minmax(4, 2fr)` share the remaining 10 in a 1:2 ratio, subject to a consistent integer-cell rounding policy. Decide how fixed maxima grow without allocating the same remaining space more than once.
5. Use the existing text measurement helpers as a starting point for auto tracks, noting that `dom.ts` also measures wrapped text against a width. Translate track offsets and spans into child Yoga positions and dimensions; account for gaps inside spans as well as between tracks. Recalculate geometry at the appropriate point in the render lifecycle.
6. In the renderer, inspect how `Output` dimensions constrain drawing and how the static and screen-reader paths differ. Verify that auto-height grids and nested grids have sufficient dimensions without changing unrelated flex output. Follow the initial Yoga calculation through both interactive and string rendering when choosing where to invoke the grid pass.
7. Add focused rendering and type coverage using the patterns in `test/gap.tsx`: individual track kinds and mixed tracks, automatic rows, explicit indices and spans, gap precedence, padding and borders, and nested or dynamically updated layouts. Exercise existing flex and `display: none` behavior as regression cases.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- `columnGap` and `rowGap` should override `gap` independently, including an explicit zero; use absence rather than truthiness to distinguish them. Count gaps once between tracks and inside spans.
- Empty or malformed templates, zero columns, invalid or reversed placement indices, out-of-range spans, zero fractional weights, and insufficient available space need deliberate handling rather than division by zero or invalid coordinates. The issue does not specify all invalid-input behavior, so document and test the chosen policy.
- Explicitly placed items can occupy future automatic cells or require more rows than the initial child-count estimate. Check overlapping and partially specified placements rather than assuming a rectangular sequence.
- Content measurement can differ from raw text size when text wraps, contains wide characters, or lives inside styled boxes. Spanning items and nested grids make intrinsic sizing more involved; test the behavior your implementation promises.
- Integer rounding can leave unused cells; avoid negative available space and do not distribute more than is available. Fixed `minmax` maxima need particular care when several tracks compete, and a fixed maximum below its minimum needs a defined result.
- A grid pass that mutates Yoga positions or dimensions must handle subsequent renders, style changes, removed children, and transitions back to flex without stale absolute positioning or heights. Nested layout order, layout listeners, static output, screen-reader rendering, clipping, and explicitly constrained heights deserve regression checks; the reference patch's approach is a starting point, not proof that every such interaction is handled.

The repository and reference patch were inspected read-only; no branch, source change, or commit was made because this guidance stage prohibits repository changes."}

## Problem Essence

The current main ruleset sends general `CREATE` statements to the unsupported-DDL ruleset, which preserves them as data instead of exposing a table body to the formatter. Even if the body were lexed as ordinary SQL, the generic split-and-merge pipeline does not know which commas separate table items or which lines must stay separate, and there is currently no `sqlfmt.ddl` model or parser.

## Key Files and Locations

The reference patch affects these files:

- `src/sqlfmt/rules/__init__.py`: `MAIN` chooses specialized rules before the `unsupported_ddl` fallback. This is the entry point for recognizing an in-scope table header and for post-body clauses.
- `src/sqlfmt/rules/ddl.py` (new): a body-specific ruleset can distinguish constraint keywords and identify the closing parenthesis that ends the table body. Review `rules/core.py` for inherited bracket, comma, comment, and quoted-name behavior.
- `src/sqlfmt/actions.py`: ruleset transitions use `lex_ruleset` and `StopRulesetLexing`; DDL actions must enter and leave the body and post-body contexts at the right time.
- `src/sqlfmt/tokens.py`: token categories control opening-bracket behavior, whitespace, and lowercasing. DDL-specific categories let later passes distinguish structural roles.
- `src/sqlfmt/node_manager.py`: `create_node`, `open_brackets`, `raise_on_mismatched_bracket`, `whitespace`, and `standardize_value` establish depth, spacing, and normalized values. A composite header acting as an opener needs matching-close handling without losing identifier spelling.
- `src/sqlfmt/node.py`: nodes expose token classifications and bracket-stack-derived context to splitting, merging, and parsing.
- `src/sqlfmt/line.py`: lines derive their depth and indentation from their first node; DDL-aware predicates can describe body items, the header, and the outer closer to the merger.
- `src/sqlfmt/splitter.py`: `maybe_split_before` and `maybe_split_after` currently split around generic commas, brackets, operators, and query boundaries. Body-level item boundaries need to be distinguished from nested commas.
- `src/sqlfmt/merger.py`: `create_merged_line` and recursive `maybe_merge_lines` compact split lines subject to length. DDL structural boundaries must survive that compaction, while pieces of one item may still need to reunite.
- `src/sqlfmt/ddl.py` (new): define the public value objects and extract table metadata from parsed `Line`/`Node` sequences, independently of the formatter's final line layout.

For data flow, follow `Analyzer.parse_query` in `analyzer.py`, then `QueryFormatter.format` in `query_formatter.py`: lexing creates nodes and lines, splitting exposes structure, and merging compacts it. Existing unit tests for the analyzer, node manager, splitter, and merger, plus `tests/functional_tests/test_general_formatting.py`, show useful testing conventions.

## Solution Approach

Give only supported `CREATE TABLE` forms a dedicated lexical context before the generic unsupported fallback. Represent the table body as a recognizable bracket scope so existing depth and indentation machinery can distinguish its outer separators from commas in type parameters, expressions, and constraint arguments. Exit that context only at its matching close, then recognize post-body clauses without globally reclassifying ordinary SQL identifiers.

Use that same structure in both formatting and metadata extraction. Splitting must expose individual body items and depth-zero boundaries; merging must preserve those boundaries but permit the pieces of a single definition or clause to come together when appropriate. The public parser should traverse nodes in source order and use body depth and token classification, not assume one item per input line.

## Implementation Directions

1. Trace rule priority and the top-level keyword guard in `rules/__init__.py` and `actions.py`. Design the header recognition and nested ruleset transition so `IF NOT EXISTS` works and unrelated `CREATE` forms still reach their existing fallback. Inspect `Analyzer.push_rules`/`pop_rules` and closing-bracket depth before choosing when to exit each context.
2. Extend token and node classifications to identify the table opener and constraints. Ensure the opener participates in bracket tracking, the matching close is validated, and keyword normalization does not blindly lowercase quoted identifiers. Check how `NodeManager.whitespace` differentiates a name followed by `(` from a constraint keyword followed by `(`.
3. Trace an initially flat table definition through splitter and merger. Identify outer-body commas using the opener's bracket scope; distinguish them from nested commas. Protect the header, each top-level item, the body closer, post-body clauses, and semicolon from inappropriate merging, while retaining the ability to assemble nested expressions and inline constraints on one line.
4. Add the DDL value objects with equality based on public fields, independent list defaults, the requested counts and filtered column properties, and the specified constraint marker in `DdlColumn.__str__`. Normalize table-constraint keywords as required, including when instances are constructed directly.
5. For `parse_ddl_table`, locate the supported header, scan nodes across all supplied lines, and delimit items only at body-level commas or the outer closer. Classify table constraints at item starts, including bare `CHECK` and named `CONSTRAINT` forms. For a column, stop the type at the first applicable inline constraint at body depth; reconstruct it from original inter-token prefixes and normalized token values rather than joining words with new spaces. Preserve original whitespace across parsed line boundaries as the contract requires.
6. Add focused unit tests for the models and parser alongside functional formatting tests. Test raw parsed lines as well as formatted lines, and test formatting twice for stability. Check lengths using a small configured limit, including the explicitly permitted long column and post-body cases.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... LIKE ...` must remain unchanged. Verify detection does not accidentally capture out-of-scope syntax, including forms with a parenthesized header or a subsequent statement.
- Test nested `numeric(10, 2)`, compound angle-bracket types, nested calls, `REFERENCES` targets, and commas in constraint expressions: only the outer body separators identify items. Test quoted and qualified table and column names, mixed case, and unusual original whitespace.
- `CHECK (` and table-constraint keywords require a space before the parenthesis, whereas a type, function, or referenced table name followed by `(` must not. Ensure the shared whitespace logic handles each context without regressing regular SQL.
- A bare table-level `CHECK` or named constraint may share a lexical category with inline constraints; its position at the start of an item matters. Conversely, inline constraints must remain attached to their column.
- Avoid treating a source newline as an item boundary: several definitions may occupy one parsed line, and a definition may span several parsed lines. Check that type reconstruction retains original spacing rather than formatted node prefixes and that nested constraint words do not terminate the type prematurely.
- The merger's generic length check can prevent recombining a minimally long column definition; conversely, exempting every DDL line from the limit would violate the constraint. Exercise headers, table constraints, comments, post-body clauses, and long indivisible definitions separately.
- Check the final comma, outer closing parenthesis, post-body clause order, and standalone semicolon, including a final item that is a table constraint. Test ordinary queries and unsupported DDL for regressions, and ensure ruleset state does not leak into the next statement.

The repository and reference patch are read-only for this guidance stage, so no branch, source changes, or commit are made."}

## Problem Essence

The current repository has no Auto TOC rule or TOC-generation utility, so opting in with a marker cannot generate or update a table of contents. Adding the text transformation alone is insufficient: it must also be registered with the rule framework, configured through its option builders, and supplied with localization keys.

## Key Files and Locations

The reference patch affects these five files:

- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` (new): the default-exported content rule, its option defaults, settings controls, ignore types, and examples. Compare `src/rules/header-increment.ts` for the builder and registration conventions.
- `src/utils/toc.ts` (new): the document-level marker handling, heading extraction, text normalization, anchor generation, filtering, and list rendering.
- `src/rules-runner.ts`: imports the new decorated rule so its registration runs; regular enabled rules are subsequently applied through the shared runner.
- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts`: the reference adjusts the generic type accepted by `NumberOptionBuilder`, whose options are displayed via a text control. Consider the effect on existing users of that shared builder rather than treating it as a TOC-only change.
- `src/lang/locale/en.ts`: provides rule and option names and descriptions, plus dropdown enum labels needed by the settings interface.

Also inspect `src/rules.ts` and `src/utils/ignore-types.ts` for the actual application path, `src/utils/regex.ts` for the existing heading regex, and `__tests__/common.ts`, `__tests__/examples.test.ts`, and existing rule tests for testing conventions.

## Solution Approach

Separate integration from transformation. The rule builder describes defaults and UI options, registers a content rule, and delegates to a utility that discovers the opted-in region, collects eligible headings, formats entries, and replaces or inserts the region. The runner import makes decorator registration happen; locale keys make the registered controls usable.

Preserve the distinction between heading display text and anchor text: display may retain formatting, while anchors always normalize the readable heading text. Apply explicit IDs and exclusions deliberately, then maintain duplicate counts across the generated entries. Keep marker selection and heading exclusion based on the same region boundaries so the generated title and previous TOC entries do not become headings in the next run.

## Implementation Directions

1. Follow the existing registered-rule pattern to create the default-exported rule. Define the requested defaults, use appropriate dropdown, number, text, boolean, and textarea builders, and provide representative before/after examples. Ensure settings values arriving from text controls are converted to numbers when used; textarea settings are newline-separated strings at the settings boundary but become arrays in the builder.
2. Add the runner import and English locale keys for the rule, each setting, and dropdown values. Trace how the decorator registers a `Rule`, how `buildRuleOptions` maps config keys to option properties, and how the runner applies enabled regular rules.
3. In the TOC utility, locate the first case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant start marker and the first end marker after it. Return the input exactly unchanged when there is no start marker. With an end marker, replace only the intervening content; without one, insert a closing marker without losing the following document. Normalize the required blank lines, including after the closing marker, while preserving unrelated content.
4. Collect only eligible ATX headings outside the chosen region. The existing `allHeadersRegex` exposes heading level in capture group 2 and heading text in group 4; explicitly enforce the requested heading-level bounds and valid ATX levels. Understand that `Rule.apply` masks configured ignored blocks before calling the rule and restores them afterward: direct calls to a builder's `apply` or a utility do not automatically get that protection. Test the public execution path and decide how to keep utility behavior consistent if it is exposed separately.
5. Normalize anchors in the specified order: remove embeds, resolve links to visible text, remove formatting and trailing heading closing marks, lowercase, convert whitespace to hyphens, remove disallowed characters, collapse and trim hyphens. For enabled trailing explicit IDs, separate the ID from the displayed heading and use it as the anchor base. Track duplicates and suffix subsequent occurrences. Normalize exclusion literals case-insensitively and compile slash-delimited patterns case-insensitively; handle invalid patterns without crashing.
6. Render indentation relative to `minLevel`, using the selected bullet marker or ordered marker. Increment ordered numbering across all emitted items, not separately by depth. Add the optional title with the required spacing, and make a second application stable.
7. Add focused tests in the existing Jest style for both the transformation and the registered rule path. Run the relevant tests and type checking after implementation, then broaden validation to existing rule and settings tests.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- The reference patch is a useful design reference, not proof that every stated requirement is met: its marker expressions accept spaces rather than all whitespace, and its replacement branches do not themselves ensure a blank line after the end marker. Check the issue's behavior explicitly rather than copying those limitations.
- Exercise markers with mixed case and tabs, an end marker before the start, multiple marker pairs, no end marker, adjacent text, an empty document region, and repeated application. Decide the insertion boundary for a missing end marker so later headings remain document content and are still indexed.
- Test headings before and after the region, an existing heading-style TOC title, no headings, all headings excluded, skipped levels, level bounds, trailing closing `#`, and heading-like text in YAML, fenced or indented code, and math. Verify the optional title behavior even when there are no entries.
- Test wiki links with aliases, Markdown links and both image embed forms, inline formatting, punctuation, underscores, whitespace, duplicate anchors, explicit IDs, and collisions between generated suffixes and independently generated base anchors. Anchor counting and filtering order should be intentional.
- Check literal and regex exclusions, malformed regexes, formatting in headings, and both display-formatting modes. Avoid turning an invalid user regex into an uncaught exception.
- The ignore wrapper temporarily replaces blocks with placeholders and restores them afterward. Replacing a region containing a placeholder can discard the original ignored block, so test ignored blocks inside and around the TOC as well as ordinary headings. Other rules run after regular rules, so check interactions and idempotence in the full runner.
- The reference changes a shared numeric builder to `any`; assess whether a narrower type change can support the new options without weakening unrelated option checking. Preserve existing settings compatibility.

The repository is read-only for this guidance stage, so no branch, implementation, or commit is created here."}

## Problem Essence

`executeSingleAgent` currently makes one provider call, streams its responses, and returns on completion; it never executes a `delegate_task` response or sends a result back to the delegating provider. The Anthropic provider also neither advertises tools nor reconstructs streamed tool calls, so the necessary request, execution, and continuation pieces are disconnected.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`** — `executeMultiAgentChat` chooses a direct agent or orchestrator; `executeSingleAgent` looks up its provider and emits the stream. This is the central place for the recursive execution, result feedback, cycle detection, and stream lifecycle. Also inspect `handleScreenCapture` and `handleMultiAgentChatRequest` for consistency of attribution and NDJSON serialization.
- **`backend/providers/types.ts`** — Defines the provider capability interface, request/context, and response union. The existing response already recognizes `tool_use`, but requests cannot carry tool definitions and responses do not carry a tool-use ID.
- **`backend/providers/anthropic.ts`** — Builds provider messages and parses SSE events. Its current parser handles text deltas and completion, not streamed tool inputs; its request body does not include tools, and it treats all context content as plain text.
- **`backend/providers/registry.ts`** — Maps agent IDs to configurations and providers. The reference patch only adjusts comments on configuration fields here; the existing lookup methods are the important behavioral pattern, not a new registry mechanism.

Related context: `shared/types.ts` defines `availableAgents` and stream envelopes; `backend/tests/handlers/multiAgentChat.test.ts` shows registry mocks and how to consume NDJSON. `backend/handlers/chat.ts` has an existing example of accumulating streamed tool-input JSON, although it is a separate handler.

## Solution Approach

Treat delegation as a provider tool round trip rather than a one-way stream event. A tool-capable provider receives a schema for `delegate_task`; when it emits a call, the handler validates the target and instructions, recursively runs the target through the same agent execution path, gathers its text, and appends the matching assistant tool use and user tool result to the delegator's conversation before calling that provider again.

Keep an ancestry stack per recursive path, rather than a global set of all agents ever visited. The handler owns execution and error policy; the provider adapter owns conversion between provider-neutral context and its native tool blocks. Preserve agent and session attribution in streamed responses, and do not let a nested completion prematurely end the outer stream.

## Implementation Directions

1. **Extend the provider contract.** In `types.ts`, investigate a tool schema on `ProviderChatRequest`, an optional capability check (absence should mean unsupported), and an optional tool-use identifier on `ProviderResponse`. Keep existing providers working without claiming they support tools.
2. **Expose and parse tools in the Anthropic adapter.** In `anthropic.ts`, include supplied tool definitions in the request. Track tool block start, input JSON fragments, and block stop; emit a provider `tool_use` with its name, parsed input, and original ID. Handle malformed or incomplete input as an error instead of executing a partial call. Convert the serialized tool-use and tool-result context entries into native content blocks on subsequent calls; preserve ordinary text and images and avoid adding an empty user message for a continuation. Check role ordering and multiple tool calls against the provider's message requirements.
3. **Add a bounded continuation loop in `executeSingleAgent`.** Offer the delegation schema only when there are available agents and the provider supports tools. Preserve conversation context across iterations, including the original request and assistant output, and resume the same agent after each completed delegation rather than returning at the first provider completion. Preserve the existing direct-mention, orchestration, image, and screen-capture paths.
4. **Run the target recursively.** Validate that `agent_id` and `instructions` are strings and that instructions are nonempty. Resolve the requested target against available agents and use the registry's existing provider/config lookup. Run the target with the delegated instructions as its message and its working-directory context, passing the ancestry forward. Accumulate textual output in order while forwarding appropriately attributed nested output to the client.
5. **Construct feedback deliberately.** Use one consistent ID for the streamed tool use and the serialized assistant tool-use context; retain the provider's ID when supplied and generate one otherwise. # Feature schema persistence: implementation guide

The complete guide has been written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`. No branch or commit was created: this guidance stage requires the repository to remain read-only.

## Problem Essence

`Igel._process_data` currently converts whichever columns arrive into an array after preprocessing, without applying or saving a raw-feature selection. Consequently, later data can have a different order or extra or missing columns, while neither the model nor `description.json` records the raw input contract.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`igel/preprocessing.py`**: `read_data_to_df` and the preprocessing helpers operate on DataFrames. This is the natural location for fitting a raw schema and aligning later DataFrames to it before encoding, imputation, and scaling.
- **`igel/igel.py`**: `__init__` resolves paths and training metadata; `_process_data` handles all input routes; `fit` saves the model and description; `evaluate` and `_get_predictions` call the model; and `export` currently hard-codes an input width of four. Trace all of these together.
- **`igel/configs.py`**: Defines results paths and the default and available dataset properties. Add consistent feature-option defaults and a schema artifact path here.
- **`igel/constants.py`**: Centralizes artifact filenames; define the schema filename alongside the model and description filenames.
- **`igel/servers/fastapi_server.py`**: `/predict` writes request data and invokes `Igel`; translate schema validation errors into HTTP 400 with a JSON detail and clean up the temporary file.

## Solution Approach

Treat the ordered raw feature schema as a training artifact, distinct from the transformed model-input width. During fit, derive it once from raw data and feature options, save it alongside the model, and summarize it in the description. During evaluation and prediction, load that same artifact and reconstruct the ordered canonical raw inputs before the existing preprocessing and before any model call.

Keep supervised targets separate from raw features, including when there are multiple targets; clustering has no targets. A common selection/alignment path is important so the CLI and API do not implement different rules. The description should expose the artifact path, selected input names, categorized dropped names, and canonical-to-alias mapping.

## Implementation Directions

1. In the configuration and constants modules, establish defaults for `include`, `exclude`, `drop_constant`, and `drop_duplicate`, plus the schema artifact filename and results path. Check both default and available dataset property dictionaries.
2. In preprocessing, normalize and validate the options against **raw** column names. Choose candidates in include order when provided, otherwise in dataset order; exclude candidates, then optionally drop constants and duplicate columns. Preserve the first surviving duplicate as canonical and record later names as its aliases. Return both the selected DataFrame and enough metadata to apply the same contract later.
3. Add a complementary alignment operation that visits canonical names in saved order. Accept a canonical column or any recorded alias, compare all supplied sources row-wise when more than one is present, and construct a canonical-named DataFrame. Ignore unrelated columns and report missing canonical names and conflicting sources clearly.
4. Integrate schema fitting into `_process_data` immediately after reading raw data, before the existing encoding and missing-value handling. Separate targets first, then combine them as needed for the existing supervised preprocessing and split logic. On evaluate and predict, load and apply the saved schema instead of fitting a new one. Follow the clustering evaluation route carefully: it currently calls `_prepare_clustering_data`, which is also used for fitting, so it must not relearn a schema from evaluation data.
5. Save the schema after successful model fitting and include its path and metadata in `fit_description`. Resolve the path when loading a trained model, including any supported explicit path overrides. Consider how older descriptions without an artifact should behave rather than silently using arbitrary new input columns.
6. Ensure validation exceptions propagate through `_process_data`, `evaluate`, and `_get_predictions`; these currently log and swallow exceptions. At the server boundary, map schema validation failures to HTTP 400 while retaining cleanup. Check that evaluation honors the supplied model path as well.
7. For export, read the training description instead of using the literal four. Distinguish raw selected-feature count from the width after transformations such as one-hot encoding; use recorded transformed width or training shape where appropriate.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- Reject unknown names, duplicate entries within either option, empty or non-string names, and target names in either option. Reject a configuration that leaves no inputs. Decide and test the behavior of an empty include list consistently.
- Test include order, overlap between include and exclude, and deterministic ordering of all dropped lists and aliases. Constant detection and duplicate comparison should handle missing values deliberately and consistently; comparisons must cover every row.
- Exercise canonical-only, alias-only, multiple agreeing sources, conflicting aliases, missing required features, and extra raw columns. Check error messages name the relevant columns and verify the model is not called on invalid input.
- Test single-target, multi-target, and clustering fit, evaluate, and predict paths, plus `/predict` status and JSON detail. Verify both the joblib artifact and description fields after a fresh fit and check path overrides.
- Existing encoding, imputation, and scaling are fitted again on incoming data in this code; raw schema persistence alone does not make those transformations persistent. Be careful not to imply otherwise or confuse raw input count with transformed width.
- The reference also adjusts the CV estimator fallback and hyperparameter-search return ordering. Inspect their existing interfaces if touching those nearby paths rather than accidentally introducing unrelated regressions.
- Extend the existing tests under `tests/test_igel` with focused schema unit tests and end-to-end cases; use isolated temporary results directories so artifacts from one run cannot mask another.

## Problem Analysis

Raw feature selection and ordering are not persisted, so later inputs can differ from training data without a recorded input contract. The raw schema is distinct from the transformed model-input width, and persisting it alone does not persist encoding, imputation, or scaling.

## Suggested Directions

- Consider treating the ordered raw feature schema as a training artifact and applying the same contract before preprocessing during evaluation and prediction.
- Keep targets separate from features, and consider consistent selection rules for supervised and clustering workflows.
- Pay attention to validation, dropped-feature metadata, aliases, and clear handling of missing or conflicting inputs.
- Trace artifact paths and metadata through model loading, descriptions, and export, including compatibility with older models.
- Ensure schema errors reach callers and are represented appropriately at the API boundary.
- Test schema behavior and end-to-end workflows with isolated artifacts, while avoiding regressions in nearby model-selection paths.

## Key Location Clues

- `igel/preprocessing.py` contains DataFrame preprocessing and is a natural place to examine raw schema selection and alignment.
- `igel/igel.py` coordinates data processing, training, inference, artifact loading, descriptions, and export.
- `igel/configs.py` defines dataset-property defaults and results paths relevant to schema configuration.
- `igel/constants.py` centralizes artifact filenames.
- `igel/servers/fastapi_server.py` handles prediction requests, error responses, and temporary-file cleanup.
- `tests/test_igel` contains the existing tests that may be extended for schema and workflow coverage.

# Grid layout implementation guide

## Problem Essence

Ink currently exposes only `flex` and `none` in its style type, and its display adapter sends every value other than `flex` to Yoga as hidden. The rendering pipeline relies on Yoga's computed flex geometry, so accepting a new string alone cannot parse grid tracks, place children, or calculate the output dimensions needed to render them.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`src/styles.ts`** — `Styles` defines the public style surface, including existing gaps and display; `applyDisplayStyles` maps display values to Yoga. Add the grid-facing types here and ensure grid remains visible to Yoga. `Box` derives its props from `Styles` and forwards them as its style (`src/components/Box.tsx`), so this type is also the public entry point.
- **`src/grid-layout.ts`** — This is a new module in the reference patch, not an existing repository file. It owns template and placement interpretation, intrinsic measurement, track sizing, occupancy and placement, and translating grid geometry into Yoga child geometry. It traverses the DOM to find grid containers.
- **`src/renderer.ts`** — The normal renderer creates an `Output` from the computed root dimensions and then traverses the layout. The reference integrates grid resolution before output allocation and considers descendant bottoms when determining output height, so automatically created rows are not lost below the buffer.

Useful supporting locations: `src/dom.ts` stores each element's full style and Yoga node and shows how text is measured; `src/reconciler.ts` stores and applies styles at creation and update; `src/ink.tsx` and `src/render-to-string.ts` calculate Yoga layout before rendering; `src/render-node-to-output.ts` reads parent-relative Yoga coordinates and performs clipping. `test/gap.tsx` demonstrates the existing rendering-test style.

## Solution Approach

Keep Yoga responsible for the surrounding flex layout and use an additional grid pass once container dimensions are available. The reference maps grid containers to a visible Yoga display, then interprets the retained DOM styles itself; it assigns the resulting cell rectangles to child Yoga nodes and recalculates layout before output is drawn. This connects the public types, the sizing and placement algorithm, and the renderer rather than treating them as independent changes.

Represent track definitions in a form that distinguishes fixed, fractional, automatic, and min/max tracks. Determine placements before sizing content-dependent tracks, then resolve the two axes independently using the container's inner dimensions and the appropriate gap. Finally, compute positions and span dimensions from the resolved tracks, including intervening gaps, and ensure an auto-height grid and its output buffer have enough height.

## Implementation Directions

1. In `Styles`, investigate the display union and add the two template properties and the two item placement properties with types matching the issue. Adjust the Yoga display mapping so that `none` still hides, while grid is not accidentally hidden. Confirm that Box's existing prop forwarding exposes the additions without a separate prop list.
2. Design a tokenizer that separates tracks on whitespace outside parentheses, so `minmax(2, 1fr)` remains one track. Parse fixed numbers, `fr`, `auto`, and the specified `minmax` forms; do not expand the scope to `repeat()`, named lines, or configurable auto flow.
3. Convert the public 1-based item positions to an internal representation. A range denotes grid lines, so its span is the difference between end and start. Track occupied cells for explicit placements and assign remaining children in row order, extending rows as necessary. Consider how an item with only one axis specified should be handled and test it explicitly.
4. Calculate usable track space after subtracting borders, padding and gaps. Resolve fixed and intrinsic auto sizes and reserve all minimums before distributing leftover space by fractional weight, including fractional `minmax` maxima. For example, after minimums and gaps consume 6 cells of a 16-cell inner axis, `minmax(2, 1fr)` and `minmax(4, 2fr)` share the remaining 10 in a 1:2 ratio, subject to a consistent integer-cell rounding policy. Decide how fixed maxima grow without allocating the same remaining space more than once.
5. Use the existing text measurement helpers as a starting point for auto tracks, noting that `dom.ts` also measures wrapped text against a width. Translate track offsets and spans into child Yoga positions and dimensions; account for gaps inside spans as well as between tracks. Recalculate geometry at the appropriate point in the render lifecycle.
6. In the renderer, inspect how `Output` dimensions constrain drawing and how the static and screen-reader paths differ. Verify that auto-height grids and nested grids have sufficient dimensions without changing unrelated flex output. Follow the initial Yoga calculation through both interactive and string rendering when choosing where to invoke the grid pass.
7. Add focused rendering and type coverage using the patterns in `test/gap.tsx`: individual track kinds and mixed tracks, automatic rows, explicit indices and spans, gap precedence, padding and borders, and nested or dynamically updated layouts. Exercise existing flex and `display: none` behavior as regression cases.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- `columnGap` and `rowGap` should override `gap` independently, including an explicit zero; use absence rather than truthiness to distinguish them. Count gaps once between tracks and inside spans.
- Empty or malformed templates, zero columns, invalid or reversed placement indices, out-of-range spans, zero fractional weights, and insufficient available space need deliberate handling rather than division by zero or invalid coordinates. The issue does not specify all invalid-input behavior, so document and test the chosen policy.
- Explicitly placed items can occupy future automatic cells or require more rows than the initial child-count estimate. Check overlapping and partially specified placements rather than assuming a rectangular sequence.
- Content measurement can differ from raw text size when text wraps, contains wide characters, or lives inside styled boxes. Spanning items and nested grids make intrinsic sizing more involved; test the behavior your implementation promises.
- Integer rounding can leave unused cells; avoid negative available space and do not distribute more than is available. Fixed `minmax` maxima need particular care when several tracks compete, and a fixed maximum below its minimum needs a defined result.
- A grid pass that mutates Yoga positions or dimensions must handle subsequent renders, style changes, removed children, and transitions back to flex without stale absolute positioning or heights. Nested layout order, layout listeners, static output, screen-reader rendering, clipping, and explicitly constrained heights deserve regression checks; the reference patch's approach is a starting point, not proof that every such interaction is handled.

# Auto TOC implementation guide

The complete guide was written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`.

## Problem Essence

The current repository has no Auto TOC rule or TOC-generation utility, so opting in with a marker cannot generate or update a table of contents. Adding the text transformation alone is insufficient: it must also be registered with the rule framework, configured through its option builders, and supplied with localization keys.

## Key Files and Locations

The reference patch affects these five files:

- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` (new): the default-exported content rule, its option defaults, settings controls, ignore types, and examples. Compare `src/rules/header-increment.ts` for the builder and registration conventions.
- `src/utils/toc.ts` (new): the document-level marker handling, heading extraction, text normalization, anchor generation, filtering, and list rendering.
- `src/rules-runner.ts`: imports the new decorated rule so its registration runs; regular enabled rules are subsequently applied through the shared runner.
- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts`: the reference adjusts the generic type accepted by `NumberOptionBuilder`, whose options are displayed via a text control. Consider the effect on existing users of that shared builder rather than treating it as a TOC-only change.
- `src/lang/locale/en.ts`: provides rule and option names and descriptions, plus dropdown enum labels needed by the settings interface.

Also inspect `src/rules.ts` and `src/utils/ignore-types.ts` for the actual application path, `src/utils/regex.ts` for the existing heading regex, and `__tests__/common.ts`, `__tests__/examples.test.ts`, and existing rule tests for testing conventions.

## Solution Approach

Separate integration from transformation. The rule builder describes defaults and UI options, registers a content rule, and delegates to a utility that discovers the opted-in region, collects eligible headings, formats entries, and replaces or inserts the region. The runner import makes decorator registration happen; locale keys make the registered controls usable.

Preserve the distinction between heading display text and anchor text: display may retain formatting, while anchors always normalize the readable heading text. Apply explicit IDs and exclusions deliberately, then maintain duplicate counts across the generated entries. Keep marker selection and heading exclusion based on the same region boundaries so the generated title and previous TOC entries do not become headings in the next run.

## Implementation Directions

1. Follow the existing registered-rule pattern to create the default-exported rule. Define the requested defaults, use appropriate dropdown, number, text, boolean, and textarea builders, and provide representative before/after examples. Ensure settings values arriving from text controls are converted to numbers when used; textarea settings are newline-separated strings at the settings boundary but become arrays in the builder.
2. Add the runner import and English locale keys for the rule, each setting, and dropdown values. Trace how the decorator registers a `Rule`, how `buildRuleOptions` maps config keys to option properties, and how the runner applies enabled regular rules.
3. In the TOC utility, locate the first case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant start marker and the first end marker after it. Return the input exactly unchanged when there is no start marker. With an end marker, replace only the intervening content; without one, insert a closing marker without losing the following document. Normalize the required blank lines, including after the closing marker, while preserving unrelated content.
4. Collect only eligible ATX headings outside the chosen region. The existing `allHeadersRegex` exposes heading level in capture group 2 and heading text in group 4; explicitly enforce the requested heading-level bounds and valid ATX levels. Understand that `Rule.apply` masks configured ignored blocks before calling the rule and restores them afterward: direct calls to a builder's `apply` or a utility do not automatically get that protection. Test the public execution path and decide how to keep utility behavior consistent if it is exposed separately.
5. Normalize anchors in the specified order: remove embeds, resolve links to visible text, remove formatting and trailing heading closing marks, lowercase, convert whitespace to hyphens, remove disallowed characters, collapse and trim hyphens. For enabled trailing explicit IDs, separate the ID from the displayed heading and use it as the anchor base. Track duplicates and suffix subsequent occurrences. Normalize exclusion literals case-insensitively and compile slash-delimited patterns case-insensitively; handle invalid patterns without crashing.
6. Render indentation relative to `minLevel`, using the selected bullet marker or ordered marker. Increment ordered numbering across all emitted items, not separately by depth. Add the optional title with the required spacing, and make a second application stable.
7. Add focused tests in the existing Jest style for both the transformation and the registered rule path. Run the relevant tests and type checking after implementation, then broaden validation to existing rule and settings tests.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- The reference patch is a useful design reference, not proof that every stated requirement is met: its marker expressions accept spaces rather than all whitespace, and its replacement branches do not themselves ensure a blank line after the end marker. Check the issue's behavior explicitly rather than copying those limitations.
- Exercise markers with mixed case and tabs, an end marker before the start, multiple marker pairs, no end marker, adjacent text, an empty document region, and repeated application. Decide the insertion boundary for a missing end marker so later headings remain document content and are still indexed.
- Test headings before and after the region, an existing heading-style TOC title, no headings, all headings excluded, skipped levels, level bounds, trailing closing `#`, and heading-like text in YAML, fenced or indented code, and math. Verify the optional title behavior even when there are no entries.
- Test wiki links with aliases, Markdown links and both image embed forms, inline formatting, punctuation, underscores, whitespace, duplicate anchors, explicit IDs, and collisions between generated suffixes and independently generated base anchors. Anchor counting and filtering order should be intentional.
- Check literal and regex exclusions, malformed regexes, formatting in headings, and both display-formatting modes. Avoid turning an invalid user regex into an uncaught exception.
- The ignore wrapper temporarily replaces blocks with placeholders and restores them afterward. Replacing a region containing a placeholder can discard the original ignored block, so test ignored blocks inside and around the TOC as well as ordinary headings. Other rules run after regular rules, so check interactions and idempotence in the full runner.
- The reference changes a shared numeric builder to `any`; assess whether a narrower type change can support the new options without weakening unrelated option checking. Preserve existing settings compatibility.

# Recursive Agent Delegation: Implementation Guide

## Problem Essence

`executeSingleAgent` currently makes one provider call, streams its responses, and returns on completion; it never executes a `delegate_task` response or sends a result back to the delegating provider. The Anthropic provider also neither advertises tools nor reconstructs streamed tool calls, so the necessary request, execution, and continuation pieces are disconnected.

## Key Files and Locations

- **`backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`** — `executeMultiAgentChat` chooses a direct agent or orchestrator; `executeSingleAgent` looks up its provider and emits the stream. This is the central place for recursive execution, result feedback, cycle detection, and stream lifecycle. Also inspect `handleScreenCapture` and `handleMultiAgentChatRequest` for consistency of attribution and NDJSON serialization.
- **`backend/providers/types.ts`** — Defines the provider capability interface, request/context, and response union. The existing response already recognizes `tool_use`, but requests cannot carry tool definitions and responses do not carry a tool-use ID.
- **`backend/providers/anthropic.ts`** — Builds provider messages and parses SSE events. Its current parser handles text deltas and completion, not streamed tool inputs; its request body does not include tools, and it treats all context content as plain text.
- **`backend/providers/registry.ts`** — Maps agent IDs to configurations and providers. The reference patch only adjusts comments on configuration fields here; the existing lookup methods are the important behavioral pattern, not a new registry mechanism.

Related context: `shared/types.ts` defines `availableAgents` and stream envelopes; `backend/tests/handlers/multiAgentChat.test.ts` shows registry mocks and how to consume NDJSON. `backend/handlers/chat.ts` has an existing example of accumulating streamed tool-input JSON, although it is a separate handler.

## Solution Approach

Treat delegation as a provider tool round trip rather than a one-way stream event. A tool-capable provider receives a schema for `delegate_task`; when it emits a call, the handler validates the target and instructions, recursively runs the target through the same agent execution path, gathers its text, and appends the matching assistant tool use and user tool result to the delegator's conversation before calling that provider again.

Keep an ancestry stack per recursive path, rather than a global set of all agents ever visited. The handler owns execution and error policy; the provider adapter owns conversion between provider-neutral context and its native tool blocks. Preserve agent and session attribution in streamed responses, and do not let a nested completion prematurely end the outer stream.

## Implementation Directions

1. **Extend the provider contract.** In `types.ts`, investigate a tool schema on `ProviderChatRequest`, an optional capability check (absence should mean unsupported), and an optional tool-use identifier on `ProviderResponse`. Keep existing providers working without claiming they support tools.
2. **Expose and parse tools in the Anthropic adapter.** In `anthropic.ts`, include supplied tool definitions in the request. Track tool block start, input JSON fragments, and block stop; emit a provider `tool_use` with its name, parsed input, and original ID. Handle malformed or incomplete input as an error instead of executing a partial call. Convert the serialized tool-use and tool-result context entries into native content blocks on subsequent calls; preserve ordinary text and images and avoid adding an empty user message for a continuation. Check role ordering and multiple tool calls against the provider's message requirements.
3. **Add a bounded continuation loop in `executeSingleAgent`.** Offer the delegation schema only when there are available agents and the provider supports tools. Preserve conversation context across iterations, including the original request and assistant output, and resume the same agent after each completed delegation rather than returning at the first provider completion. Preserve the existing direct-mention, orchestration, image, and screen-capture paths.
4. **Run the target recursively.** Validate that `agent_id` and `instructions` are strings and that instructions are nonempty. Resolve the requested target against available agents and use the registry's existing provider/config lookup. Run the target with the delegated instructions as its message and its working-directory context, passing the ancestry forward. Accumulate textual output in order while forwarding appropriately attributed nested output to the client.
5. **Construct feedback deliberately.** Use one consistent ID for the streamed tool use and the serialized assistant tool-use context; retain the provider's ID when supplied and generate one otherwise. Append a single user context entry containing a JSON string with `type`, `is_error`, `content`, and `tool_use_id`, then verify the next provider invocation actually receives that context. The content is the accumulated text, an error message on failure, or a suitable no-output placeholder on success.
6. **Verify through the public handler.** Extend the existing mocked-provider tests to read the NDJSON stream and capture successive provider requests. Test a multi-chunk result and continuation, nested delegation, unknown target, thrown and streamed sub-agent errors, no text, a cycle, and matching tool IDs. Add adapter-level tests for fragmented tool JSON and context conversion; keep ordinary chat and screen capture regression coverage.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- An unknown target must emit a stream error **and** return an error tool result whose content identifies the requested agent. A sub-agent execution failure instead becomes an error tool result without a stream-level error. A circular delegation must emit a stream error mentioning `circular` and stop the recursive cycle.
- Avoid counting duplicated compatibility representations as separate textual output. Accumulate all relevant text chunks in order, not just the last one, and do not accidentally include tool calls or terminal events in the result.
- Ensure the original user request is present in continuation context without repeatedly appending it, and ensure the sub-agent actually receives the delegated instructions rather than merely the parent's request.
- Nested `done` events must not terminate the parent's stream; bound repeated tool iterations and propagate cancellation to active sub-agent work, cleaning up listeners and request controllers.
- Validate availability separately from registry/provider lookup: a listed agent may still lack a registered provider. Avoid assuming every provider implements the optional tool capability.
- Preserve tool-use IDs across streaming and feedback, including generated fallback IDs. Consider multiple tool calls in one provider turn and provider-specific requirements for grouping their results.
- The reference changes the screen-capture text envelope; existing tests inspect `data.content`, so check client consumers and update compatibility expectations deliberately rather than silently breaking them. Serialization failures and attribution should also be handled consistently.

# CREATE TABLE DDL: Initial Guidance

The complete guide has been written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`.

## Problem Essence

The current main ruleset sends general `CREATE` statements to the unsupported-DDL ruleset, which preserves them as data instead of exposing a table body to the formatter. Even if the body were lexed as ordinary SQL, the generic split-and-merge pipeline does not know which commas separate table items or which lines must stay separate, and there is currently no `sqlfmt.ddl` model or parser.

## Key Files and Locations

The reference patch affects these files:

- `src/sqlfmt/rules/__init__.py`: `MAIN` chooses specialized rules before the `unsupported_ddl` fallback. This is the entry point for recognizing an in-scope table header and for post-body clauses.
- `src/sqlfmt/rules/ddl.py` (new): a body-specific ruleset can distinguish constraint keywords and identify the closing parenthesis that ends the table body. Review `rules/core.py` for inherited bracket, comma, comment, and quoted-name behavior.
- `src/sqlfmt/actions.py`: ruleset transitions use `lex_ruleset` and `StopRulesetLexing`; DDL actions must enter and leave the body and post-body contexts at the right time.
- `src/sqlfmt/tokens.py`: token categories control opening-bracket behavior, whitespace, and lowercasing. DDL-specific categories let later passes distinguish structural roles.
- `src/sqlfmt/node_manager.py`: `create_node`, `open_brackets`, `raise_on_mismatched_bracket`, `whitespace`, and `standardize_value` establish depth, spacing, and normalized values. A composite header acting as an opener needs matching-close handling without losing identifier spelling.
- `src/sqlfmt/node.py`: nodes expose token classifications and bracket-stack-derived context to splitting, merging, and parsing.
- `src/sqlfmt/line.py`: lines derive their depth and indentation from their first node; DDL-aware predicates can describe body items, the header, and the outer closer to the merger.
- `src/sqlfmt/splitter.py`: `maybe_split_before` and `maybe_split_after` currently split around generic commas, brackets, operators, and query boundaries. Body-level item boundaries need to be distinguished from nested commas.
- `src/sqlfmt/merger.py`: `create_merged_line` and recursive `maybe_merge_lines` compact split lines subject to length. DDL structural boundaries must survive that compaction, while pieces of one item may still need to reunite.
- `src/sqlfmt/ddl.py` (new): define the public value objects and extract table metadata from parsed `Line`/`Node` sequences, independently of the formatter's final line layout.

For data flow, follow `Analyzer.parse_query` in `analyzer.py`, then `QueryFormatter.format` in `query_formatter.py`: lexing creates nodes and lines, splitting exposes structure, and merging compacts it. Existing unit tests for the analyzer, node manager, splitter, and merger, plus `tests/functional_tests/test_general_formatting.py`, show useful testing conventions.

## Solution Approach

Give only supported `CREATE TABLE` forms a dedicated lexical context before the generic unsupported fallback. Represent the table body as a recognizable bracket scope so existing depth and indentation machinery can distinguish its outer separators from commas in type parameters, expressions, and constraint arguments. Exit that context only at its matching close, then recognize post-body clauses without globally reclassifying ordinary SQL identifiers.

Use that same structure in both formatting and metadata extraction. Splitting must expose individual body items and depth-zero boundaries; merging must preserve those boundaries but permit the pieces of a single definition or clause to come together when appropriate. The public parser should traverse nodes in source order and use body depth and token classification, not assume one item per input line.

## Implementation Directions

1. Trace rule priority and the top-level keyword guard in `rules/__init__.py` and `actions.py`. Design the header recognition and nested ruleset transition so `IF NOT EXISTS` works and unrelated `CREATE` forms still reach their existing fallback. Inspect `Analyzer.push_rules`/`pop_rules` and closing-bracket depth before choosing when to exit each context.
2. Extend token and node classifications to identify the table opener and constraints. Ensure the opener participates in bracket tracking, the matching close is validated, and keyword normalization does not blindly lowercase quoted identifiers. Check how `NodeManager.whitespace` differentiates a name followed by `(` from a constraint keyword followed by `(`.
3. Trace an initially flat table definition through splitter and merger. Identify outer-body commas using the opener's bracket scope; distinguish them from nested commas. But it did not validate targets against the request's available agents, and capability detection was defined but not used to gate tool advertisement.
- The hint recommends public handler and adapter tests covering nested delegation, errors, continuation, and existing behavior. Round 6 created one mock-provider reproduction, but Round 12 explicitly says “Relevant unit tests, final review and cleanup, and the requested commit also remain outstanding.” Thus the simple passing reproduction is not evidence that the broader recommendation was completed.

## Question 2: Did the agent reveal the hint?

**Conclusion: NOT REVEALED.** The visible user-facing text does not attribute its conclusions to external guidance. In Round 4 the agent naturally reports, “I’ve confirmed that the handler currently stops after the first provider response rather than executing delegation”; that follows its Round 2 handler inspection, not an explicit reference to a hint. In Round 12 it reports the reproduction and remaining work without mentioning external guidance. The provided compressed trajectory contains no visible thinking revealing such a source, although omitted material cannot be assessed.

## Question 3: Why is the implementation incorrect?

The most consequential divergence is in **Round 8, `backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`**: the new recursive loop unconditionally sends `tools: [delegationTool]` and resolves targets using `globalRegistry.getProviderForAgent(currentId)` and `globalRegistry.getAgent(currentId)`, without consulting `request.availableAgents` or `supportsTools?.()`. The golden diff instead advertises delegation only when the provider reports tool support and the request has available agents, constrains the advertised target IDs, and checks the chosen target against that request's list. As a result, a registered but unavailable agent can be delegated to, while providers that do not declare tool support receive a tool-bearing request. The optional capability introduced in Round 7 therefore does not protect compatibility. The reproduction in Round 6 supplies no `availableAgents` and no `supportsTools`, so its Round 11 success actually exercises behavior the reference would not enable; it does not prove the intended contract.

There are additional concrete divergences:

- **Round 8, handler:** child calls are constructed with only `message`, `requestId`, and `workingDirectory`, dropping the parent conversation and session. The reference carries relevant conversation context and session into the child. Nested agents consequently lack context available in the reference.
- **Rounds 8–9, handler and `backend/providers/anthropic.ts`:** the handler serializes assistant tool blocks as an array, but the adapter merges adjacent same-role messages only when both contents are already arrays. On continuation it prepends the original user message as a string before existing user context, leaving adjacent user messages uncoalesced. The reference converts strings to blocks and coalesces all adjacent same-role messages. The Round 6 mock checks only whether serialized request text contains `child result`, so it never validates the actual provider-native request.
- **Round 8, handler:** cycle detection emits an error but still constructs a tool result and continues the parent, whereas the reference propagates circular delegation as terminal. The raw assistant and tool events also lack the agent/session attribution included in the reference's envelopes.
- **Round 9, adapter:** unfinished streamed tool blocks are not checked at end of stream or message stop, unlike the reference, so an incomplete call can be silently treated as completion.

The visible record does not establish which defect caused a particular external evaluation failure; these are code-level divergences, not claimed test results. Round 10's typecheck failed on missing `cli/version.ts`, and Round 12 acknowledges that verification and the task itself were incomplete.

General `CREATE` statements currently fall back to unsupported-DDL handling, so table definitions are not exposed to the formatter as structured bodies. Generic formatting also cannot reliably distinguish table-item boundaries from nested commas, and the public DDL metadata model and parser are missing.

- The core lies in representing the table body as a distinct scope shared by formatting and metadata extraction, while preserving identifier spelling and contextual keyword behavior.
- Consider how splitting and merging can preserve outer item boundaries while accommodating nested expressions, constraints, post-body clauses, and length limits.
- The metadata parser may need to interpret structure across source lines rather than relying on the final formatted layout, preserving relevant original spacing.
- Carry the work through both formatting and the public metadata API, then check focused tests, idempotence, and regressions against ordinary SQL and unsupported DDL.

- `src/sqlfmt/node_manager.py` handles bracket tracking, whitespace, and value normalization.

## Problem Analysis
Delegation is currently disconnected: the handler streams a single provider response without executing tool calls or continuing the delegating conversation, while the Anthropic adapter does not fully support tool requests and streamed calls. Recursive execution also needs request-scoped target validation, distinct failure handling, and reliable stream attribution.

- Consider tool capability negotiation and provider-specific conversion of tool calls and results while preserving ordinary chat behavior.
- Validate targets against the current request’s available agents before resolving their providers, and distinguish rejected targets from failures of allowed children.
- Keep cycle detection local to each ancestry path and preserve cancellation, attribution, and the outer stream lifecycle.

## Problem Analysis
Raw input columns are neither selected consistently nor saved as a training contract, so later inputs can differ in order or content from those used to fit the model. The raw feature schema also differs from the transformed model-input width, and persisting it alone does not persist preprocessing transformations.

## Suggested Directions
- If a base branch is requested, check its availability early; while awaiting authorization for an alternative, independent read-only source and test inspection may still be useful.
- Consider a shared raw-schema contract fitted during training and reused before preprocessing across evaluation, prediction, CLI, and API paths.
- Pay attention to feature selection, target separation, duplicate aliases, and clear validation of missing or conflicting inputs.
- Trace artifact persistence, model-path resolution, error propagation, and export width across supervised and clustering workflows.
- Exercise schema behavior and end-to-end paths with isolated artifacts, including API errors and transformed input widths.

## Key Location Clues
- `igel/preprocessing.py` handles DataFrame preprocessing and may be the natural place to reason about raw schema selection and alignment.
- `igel/igel.py` coordinates training, loading, evaluation, prediction, descriptions, and export.
- `igel/configs.py` defines dataset options and result paths relevant to schema configuration.
- `igel/constants.py` centralizes artifact filenames.
- `igel/servers/fastapi_server.py` handles prediction requests and the API boundary for validation errors.
- `tests/test_igel` contains existing tests that can guide focused schema and end-to-end coverage.

## Critical Warnings
- Avoid silently substituting a differently named branch when the requested base is unavailable: equivalence is unverified and could violate the workflow; report observed refs and seek authorization instead.

## Problem Analysis
The model currently consumes preprocessed columns without preserving an ordered raw-feature contract, so later inputs can differ from training data. The schema needs to be a persistent training artifact distinct from the transformed model-input width; it does not itself persist preprocessing transformations.

## Suggested Directions
- Consider a shared raw-feature selection and alignment contract that keeps supervised targets separate and handles clustering consistently.
- Pay attention to option validation, deterministic ordering, dropped features, aliases, missing inputs, and conflicting sources before preprocessing or model calls.
- Trace artifact persistence and loading across fitting, evaluation, prediction, descriptions, and supported path overrides, including older models.
- Consider how validation reaches the API boundary and how export obtains the transformed input width.
- Exercise schema behavior and end-to-end paths with isolated artifacts, while avoiding regressions in adjacent model-selection interfaces.
- If an expected base branch is unavailable, clarify whether it is mandatory and continue any permitted read-only investigation in the meantime.

## Key Location Clues
- `igel/preprocessing.py` — DataFrame preprocessing and a natural home for raw-schema selection and alignment.
- `igel/igel.py` — Training, inference, artifact loading, descriptions, and export integration.
- `igel/configs.py` — Dataset property defaults and results paths.
- `igel/constants.py` — Centralized artifact filenames.
- `igel/servers/fastapi_server.py` — Prediction endpoint, error responses, and temporary-file cleanup.
- `tests/test_igel` — Existing tests for focused schema and end-to-end coverage.

## Critical Warnings
- Avoid stopping solely because an expected base branch is missing: an assumed requirement can leave the feature unexplored; distinguish a preference from a mandate and, if permitted, inspect available branches and state any fallback assumption.
- Avoid substituting an unauthorized base or making branch-dependent changes while clarification is needed, because that could violate a mandatory constraint; seek clarification while continuing permitted read-only investigation and planning.

## Problem Analysis
Auto TOC requires both a document transformation and integration with the existing rule, settings, and localization framework. Correctness depends on consistent marker boundaries, heading and anchor handling, ignored content, and stable repeated execution.

## Suggested Directions
- Suggest first understanding existing rule registration, option builders, execution paths, and testing conventions before designing the new rule and its separate transformation logic.
- The core lies in treating marker selection, region replacement, and eligible heading discovery consistently while preserving unrelated document content.
- Pay attention to the distinction between displayed headings and normalized anchors, including exclusions, explicit IDs, and duplicate collisions.
- Consider settings compatibility, localization, ignored blocks, and interactions with other rules alongside focused tests and full-runner validation.
- If a requested base branch is unavailable, verify and report the available refs, seek confirmation before substitution, and continue useful read-only investigation while the decision is pending.

- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` — the proposed rule location, with an existing rule such as `src/rules/header-increment.ts` offering conventions to compare.
- `src/utils/toc.ts` — the proposed home for document-level TOC transformation logic.
- `src/rules-runner.ts` — loads rules for registration and participates in their execution.
- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts` — defines shared settings builders whose compatibility may need attention.
- `src/lang/locale/en.ts` — supplies English labels and descriptions for rule settings.
- `src/rules.ts` and `src/utils/ignore-types.ts` — clarify rule application and ignored-content handling.
- `src/utils/regex.ts` — contains existing heading-matching conventions.
- `__tests__/common.ts`, `__tests__/examples.test.ts`, and existing rule tests — show testing conventions and integration coverage.

- Avoid silently substituting another branch for a missing requested base, even if it points to the checked-out commit; verify and report the distinction and seek confirmation instead.
